cards.text: The Israelites who came back from exile have settled in their towns (Nehemiah 7:6, 73). Now all the people gather together in the square before the Water Gate. And friend, they've got a request for Ezra the scribe.

cards.question: The whole crowd in the square asks Ezra the scribe to bring something out to them. What is it?

answers.text: The Book of the Law of Moses

cards.text: So on the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brings the Law out before the assembly. Men, women, and all who can listen and understand.

cards.question: Ezra faces the square and reads the Law aloud to the crowd. How long does he keep reading?
During Ezra's long reading, the crowd stops paying attention to the Book of the Law.

cards.text: Ezra's up on a high wooden platform built for this occasion, with six men on his right and seven on his left. That's a bigger crew up front than most weddings!

cards.question: Ezra opens the book in full view of everyone, since he's up above them all. As he opens it, all the people ___.

cards.text: Then Ezra blesses the LORD, the great God. Hands go up all over the square, and the people say, “Amen, Amen!”

cards.question: After their Amen, the people bow down and worship the LORD with their faces to the ground.

cards.text: And a team of thirteen Levites goes to work, teaching the people the Law as the people stand in their places.

cards.question: As the Book of the Law is read in the square, it's also ___ so the people can understand what's being read.
As the people in the square hear the words of the Law, the whole crowd starts weeping.

cards.text: Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites tell everyone, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep.”

cards.question: Nehemiah tells the weeping crowd to go without food for the rest of the holy day.

cards.text: Nehemiah tells them to go eat what's rich and drink what's sweet. Somebody stick THAT on the fridge, because a holy day just came with a FEAST!

cards.question: Nehemiah also tells the people to send out ___ to those who have nothing prepared.
Nehemiah tells the people not to grieve on this holy day. What does he say is their strength?

cards.text: The Levites go through the crowd calming everybody down: “Be still, since today is holy. Do not grieve.”

cards.question: Then all the people eat, drink, send out portions and rejoice greatly. Why?

answers.text: They understood the words made known to them
The work on the wall was finally done
Their enemies had finally given up

cards.text: On the second day of the month, the heads of all the families, the priests and the Levites gather around Ezra the scribe. They listened for HOURS yesterday, and nobody hit snooze on day two!

cards.question: On the second day, why do the family heads, priests and Levites gather around Ezra the scribe?

answers.text: To study the words of the Law

cards.text: In the Law they find what the LORD commanded through Moses: during the feast of the seventh month, the Israelites are to dwell in booths. They're to spread the word through their towns and Jerusalem, and it starts with a trip out to the hill country.

cards.question: To make the booths, the message tells people to go out to the hill country and bring back ___.

cards.text: Olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm and other leafy trees. A whole orchard about to become somebody's walls.

cards.question: Once they have the branches, the people build booths only inside the courts of the house of God.

cards.text: Booths go up on rooftops, in courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, and in the squares by the Water Gate and by the Gate of Ephraim. You can't take ten steps without walking into somebody's living room!

cards.question: The whole assembly back from exile makes booths and lives in them. How long has it been since the Israelites celebrated like this?

answers.text: Since the days of Joshua son of Nun
Since the days of King David
Since the days of King Solomon

cards.text: From the days of Joshua son of Nun, who led Israel after Moses (Joshua 1:1-2), until that day, the Israelites hadn't celebrated like this. Since JOSHUA, and here I thought my years in the junk drawer were long!

cards.question: The whole assembly back from exile is living in booths, and there is great ___.
While the people live in booths for the feast, how often does Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God?

cards.text: The feast runs for seven days, and on the eighth day they hold an assembly.

cards.question: The Israelites hold their eighth-day assembly according to the ordinance.

cards.text: We'll stop the timer right here, friend. Jerusalem's been soaking in the Word, and Nehemiah's story still has more to tell.
